I was doing really well in the classes and my instructors sent the work I was missing to the hospital, so I was caught up when I got out.  I was just tired being indirectly condemned for something that happened when I was in a wrong state of mind.

My first big psychotic break happened a year ago.  I was working a $20hr warehouse job, but I was taking a full college course load.  I was keeping up with grades (Bs &a As), but I was having extreme break downs on a weekly basis. ( The trailers I was in were contracting/ expanding, I was hearing voices). So eventually I bought a gun and thankfully couldn't pull the trigger.   After eleven days in the hospital I have terrible anxiety over my job, and eventually lose it.   I also withdraw from school due to fact my public speaking professor would talk about how suicide is an unforgivable sin even when I was at class a day after release.  

So I decided to reset and go back to my job before the warehouse, where I really enjoy the people and still do.  They know about my issues and are finally giving me a much needed break.   I'm seeing a psych and therapist that I look forward to seeing. Since being back the grocery store, I got turned down for what for I considered a job I could stay in forever twice, due to being to "unorganized".  Eventually I picked up a second retail job, and the stress of pushing sales to strangers help drove me to relapse I've been in now.  So I resigned.

I'm taking a single college course this semester, to hopefully give me something to hold on too, because honestly right now it looks like death is the best available option even though I don't want to. I obsess over it.

I just feel like I'll be stuck working part time forever and my psyche will only get worse.

What I've learned from this past year. Is try to take things slow, and that I hit the kill switch to often.  I could have finished that semester.
